items.appliesWhen: You set --banner-ic-mt anywhere. It is a global geometry token, not a --ds-* component hook, so an app that only overrides --ds-banner-* is unaffected.
items.pitfall: Deleting the override is the whole fix, but only because the icon no longer needs nudging: it is now centred on the message block rather than aligned to the first line. If you had raised the value to line the icon up with a taller first line, that adjustment is now working against the new rule and will push the icon off centre.
items.verify: A ds-banner with two or more lines of body text shows its icon vertically centred on the text block, and no rule in your app references --banner-ic-mt.
items.restore: There is no one-line restore. `align-self: flex-start` on the icon does not reproduce the old look: it drops the one border-width of nudge the token supplied on a banner (the toast never read it — its own 2px came from a margin, removed with the same change), and a consumer's `ds-banner .icon` is specificity (0,1,1) against the component's own (0,4,0), so it does not win at all. On a `compact` banner it is actively wrong, because that variant was already centred before this change. If you must have the old alignment, fork the component's stylesheet.
items.note: The token was one border-width of optical bump, and it existed only to serve the first-line alignment rule. With the icon centred on the block there is nothing left for it to correct.
items.action: Delete any --banner-ic-mt declaration. There is no replacement token.

Build after upgrading. Rename or mark `override` every member the compiler reports as colliding, and DELETE any `startCountdown` member of yours - ours no longer exists, so yours is dead code the compiler only flags when it carries `override` (TS4113).
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends ToastRegionComponent. Template users of `<ds-toast-region>` and callers of ToastService need nothing.
items.pitfall: `startCountdown` was private in 0.11.2, so a subclass redeclaring it hit TS2415 with or without `override`. Now it is gone: a method of that name compiles clean and never runs, while one marked `override` fails with TS4113. And every one of the twelve new names is `private` or `protected`, which is no protection - a redeclared private fails with TS2415 exactly as a public collision does.
items.note: ToastRegionComponent gained the private `arm`, `pauseAll`, `resumeAll`, `syncPause`, `paused`, `remaining`, `startedAt`, `hovered`, `focusWithin`, `host` and the protected `onHover`, `onFocusWithin`, and lost `startCountdown`. A countdown is armed when a toast is promoted to visible, and re-armed from what is left when a hover or focus pause ends - the region owns the timing because only it knows when a toast became visible. None of the twelve is public API or a signal, and there is no public replacement for `startCountdown`.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS4113 / TS4114 / TS2415 / TS2416 naming ToastRegionComponent, and no `startCountdown` member remains in a subclass of it.

items.action: Change every `@include ds.color(<name>)` to one of `secondary`, `tertiary`, `error`, `success` or `warning`, or delete the include if the zone was never painting.
items.appliesWhen: Only a consumer whose own Sass calls the mixin. The `ds-color="…"` attribute in a template runs no Sass and is unaffected.
items.pitfall: This is a hard build failure, not a warning — the `@error` aborts the compile, so a wrong name that used to ship silently now stops the build. That is the point: the eleven pointers it emitted could never resolve, so the zone painted with `unset` and read as a theming problem.
items.note: `ds.color($family)` validates its argument against the five families it supports. It previously accepted any name and emitted pointers at guaranteed-invalid values.
items.verify: Your Sass compiles, and every `ds-color` zone shows its family's accent rather than falling back to the default.

informational: The banner, toast and alert icon now centres on the message block instead of aligning to the first line of text. Nothing to change: it is a visual default, applied by the components themselves. One-line messages look the same either way, which covers most toasts, except a banner with layout set to row and actions beside the text: its icon was pinned to the top of the row and now centres with the text; the difference grows with the text, and was 12px at two lines and 21px at three.

ToastService.promise() and any toast with an `action` changed their dismissal timing. A settled promise toast now counts its 4s/6s from when it becomes visible rather than from when the promise resolved, so one queued behind `maxVisible` is no longer removed before it is shown. A toast with an `action` no longer auto-dismisses at all and is always dismissible, because the region is last in tab order and the button was unreachable within the old five seconds. Hovering or focusing the region pauses every countdown. Nothing to change in consumer code; if you relied on an action toast disappearing on its own, dismiss it from the action handler.

Inside a `ds-color="error"`, `="success"` or `="warning"` zone, anything that reads the scoped accent's strong colour, --accent-strong, now renders in that status colour instead of falling back to body text — selected list and tree rows, the active sidenav item and its rail, the active tab pill, avatar initials, the active tag, dropzone text, the toast's action label, the selected toggle button, the split-button hover fill, the tonal, ghost, outline and text variants of ds-button, and the tonal variant of ds-icon-button. Nothing to change: those three families simply never defined the role the zone asked for, and --accent-strong now asks for -strong first and the family's readable on-tint -text second. A zone whose accent looked plain before will now look coloured, which is the intended appearance.
ds-banner's close button gained aria-label="Dismiss", which ds-toast and ds-alert already carried. NO ACTION.
A toast body now wraps an unbroken token instead of overflowing the pill. NO ACTION.

The toast region's hover/focus pause is derived from both sources rather than latched, so tabbing out of a region the pointer still covers does not resume, focus moving inside it is not a leave, and a toast that becomes visible while paused is banked rather than counted. A resumed toast always gets at least 600ms. NO ACTION.

ds-config and the card types moved inside the library. Every symbol still reaches the package root unchanged, and no import path of yours could have named the old location: there is one entry point and no subpath resolves into lib/. NO ACTION.

A disabled ds-accordion-item's chevron asked for a colour token this library does not define, so the declaration was invalid and the chevron inherited the surrounding colour while its label greyed correctly. It reads the disabled text colour now. NO ACTION.

The component catalogue shipped with the package names <ds-select> for the work a <ds-dropdown> would do - this library exports no such component, and an import naming it does not compile - and carries <ds-alert> with its 'neutral' variant. NO ACTION.
